markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: precision-gated, matched-target prefix cropping.** At 10% progress, prioritize an interpretable GRU4Rec experiment before adding learned history selectors.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Padding comparisons fail the declared tolerance in every category, while repeated executions match exactly. This leaves numerical execution paths and semantic defects unresolved; the recorded cuDNN TF32 setting warrants a controlled precision check [1,2]. (2) Electronics has 7.3% sampled negative-over-positive comparisons versus 1.25% for CDs_and_Vinyl. These training measurements motivate investigation but establish neither validation performance nor the value of cropping. (3) Feedback suggests that older affinity can conflict with immediate choice. Ownership, compatibility and intent remain unobserved, so recency is a hypothesis rather than an inferred label.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU biases can update states on zero inputs [1]. Padding must therefore be excluded from recurrence, rather than handled through zero embeddings alone. (2) PyTorch permits numerical differences between batched and sliced computations [2]. Tolerance failures require localization and precision controls before architectural repair. (3) Sequence-shuffling research questions how much benchmarks depend on chronology [3]. Cropping results should distinguish context removal from changes in supervised positions.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence it can provide |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding reliability | Precision and padding controls | Whether representations depend on execution layout |
| Historical context | Matched-target prefix cropping | Effect of removing context under matched suffix supervision |
| Sequence dependence | Last-item-preserving shuffle | Sensitivity to earlier ordering |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Precision-gated matched-target cropping: 4/7/5.** Originality: controlled combination, but familiar ingredients. Potential: separates two confounds, but gains are unmeasured. Difficulty: small training intervention, but candidate-pool matching requires care.
- **Last-item-preserving shuffle probe [3]: 3/6/3.** Originality: useful constrained perturbation, but established methodology. Potential: identifies order sensitivity, but introduces distribution shift. Difficulty: inexpensive frozen-model probe, but aligned targets need careful construction.
- **Jointly learned scalar hidden-state decay: 4/6/4.** Originality: economical adaptive forgetting, but standard recurrent-decay precedent. Potential: learns retention inside one network, but may overemphasize recency. Difficulty: few parameters, but recurrence and predictor changes increase verification work.

**Selected experiment.** First resolve padding discrepancies on fixed training probes using TF32-disabled and FP64 controls without relaxing tolerances retrospectively. Then compare separately trained conditions: A, unchanged full supervision; B, full context with suffix-only supervision; C, cropped context with exactly B’s suffix targets and candidate pools. Keep B’s prefix-to-suffix gradients connected. Report C−B as the controlled context-policy contrast and B−A as the supervision contrast, acknowledging residual dropout differences.

Predeclare affordable epochs, validation queries and budget allocation. Select one complete condition by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; deploy its single checkpoint per category. No validation improvement is currently established.

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic removal of old prefixes in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec using a precision gate and matched-target full-context control. Each experimental condition trains one independent model per category; deployment selects one complete condition without combining models, checkpoints or scores.
idea.motivation: The supplied measurements show repeatable but layout-dependent numerical discrepancies, including one changed ordered top-10 probe list in Industrial_and_Scientific. They do not establish padding leakage. Qualitative feedback motivates testing historical-context retention, but neither immediate intent nor harmful older history is observed. A controlled cropping experiment is appropriate at 10% research progress because it preserves the backbone and separates context changes from suffix-supervision changes.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied baseline; its implementation is not available in this writing call, so do not reconstruct its sampler or loss from assumptions. No execution or validation result is claimed.

On fixed training histories, compare aligned valid states, final features and identical candidate scores across unpadded singleton, left-padded batch, permuted batch and generated-predictor paths. Use eval/no_grad, fresh recurrent states, autocast disabled and version-supported TF32 disabling. Compare unresolved cases with an FP64 explicit recurrence using identical trained weights and PyTorch GRU equations, including all baseline transforms. Record absolute/relative discrepancies and ranking changes. Preserve the predeclared tolerance; empirical score errors are sensitivity measurements, not universal certificates. Repair padding only if a semantic defect is identified, uniformly across conditions and predictor generation. Compact real tokens before packing; never directly pack left-padded histories. Preserve aligned B×L×H outputs and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count−1.

Use p=0.5 for a crop branch; draw retained length K uniformly from ceil(n/2) through n, inclusive, and retain the final K real positions. Singleton histories remain unchanged. Generate crop plans with a dedicated RNG independent of base sampling and model/dropout randomness. B and C share exact minibatches, crop plans, targets, negative pools and optimizer schedules. Construct coupled candidate pools before applying supervision masks. Preserve B's gradient path through its full prefix. Match B/C loss reductions and positionwise regularization; retain baseline global regularization. Do not assume arbitrary objectives decompose into independent position losses.

Predeclare common E≤200, exactly 200 batches/epoch, final-epoch checkpoints, query cap and allocations within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-seconds. A complete A/B/C comparison requires twelve category-condition fits across separate trials; do not assume it is affordable. Report incomplete comparisons explicitly. Select the complete condition with highest macro validation HR@10; exact ties prefer A, B, C. No category-wise condition mixing or score fusion.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts and the pinned evaluator. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and every ModelView interface. Restore model mode after probes. Return measured metrics and definitions, marking unsupported fields unavailable. Keep full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five/category. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; do not infer unavailable attributes or access hidden tests.
idea.pseudocode:
predeclare conditions A/B/C, p=0.5, E<=200, 200 batches/epoch,
final-checkpoint rule, query cap, tie order and shared budget allocation

precision_gate(supplied_GRU4Rec):
    freeze fixed training probes; enter eval/no_grad
    compare aligned states, final features and fixed candidate scores
    across padding lengths, batch layouts and singleton execution
    repeat with supported TF32 controls and FP64 explicit recurrence
    localize recurrent, readout and predictor discrepancies
    if semantic defect confirmed: repair uniformly and verify
    if unresolved: report confound; withhold mechanistic attribution

for condition in separately_authorized_affordable_trials:
    for category in required_four_categories:
        initialize supplied corrected GRU4Rec with training seed 42
        for epoch in range(E):
            for batch_index in range(200):
                _, x, pos, neg = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
                candidates = baseline_candidates_before_masking(...)
                keep = deterministic_suffix_plan(category, epoch, batch_index)
                # Dedicated crop RNG: retain all unless crop branch is taken.
                # Crop branch retains K ~ UniformInteger(ceil(n/2), n).
                context = zero_removed_prefix(x, keep) if condition == C else x
                valid = baseline_valid_supervision(x, pos, neg)
                mask = valid if condition == A else valid & keep
                features = model.log2feats(context)
                # B keeps connected gradients through full-context prefix.
                loss = baseline_loss_with_documented_mask_reduction(
                    features, pos, candidates, mask)
                baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
        save_final_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor()
        verify_strict_reload_and_identical_input_scores()
    obtain_unchanged_host_macro_validation_HR10()

report complete C-B and B-A contrasts, counts, numerical limitations and cost
select one complete condition; deploy exactly one checkpoint/category
use full permitted history and final-nonpadding readout at inference

originality.positive: Combines numerical localization and matched suffix supervision to make a familiar context intervention easier to interpret.
originality.negative: Cropping, padding controls and matched ablations are established techniques; the contribution is experimental identification.

future_potential.positive: Can establish a reliable basis for later adaptive forgetting within one GRU network.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, and a fixed-seed sampled benchmark cannot establish general stale-interest mechanisms.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone, scoring architecture and baseline objective; masks provide compact integration points.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact candidate matching, precision diagnosis, loss-specific reductions and predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent gate equations needed for an explicit trained-weight reference.
The equations show why zero-valued padded inputs do not guarantee inert hidden states.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied corrected baseline has a padding defect.
Does not provide evidence that prefix cropping improves recommendation.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains numerical differences between batched and sliced computations and precision-dependent execution.
Supports interpreting tolerance failures through controlled numerical comparisons.
limitations: Provides no universal GRU error tolerance.
Numerical agreement alone does not validate preprocessing, causal alignment or recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: Uses sequence shuffling to investigate sequential dependence across recommendation datasets.
Motivates testing order sensitivity separately from historical-context retention.
limitations: Its findings do not establish the behavior of these four pinned Amazon tasks.
Shuffling sensitivity does not identify immediate user intent or prove that older context is harmful.
